An s3b fix-round worker grepped GLOBAL.env for credential patterns and printed the inline `postgresql://user:pass@host` DATABASE_URL line, exposing the `postgres` SUPERUSER password into its own agent transcript. Its redaction regex matched only `PASSWORD=` lines, not the inline URL form. CONTAINMENT VERIFIED BY ME, not taken on the worker's word: no tracked file in ANY of the five worktrees contains an inline credential outside workflow service definitions; the two `postgresql://postgres:***@localhost:5432/ipodhan_test` lines in the s3b ci.yml diff are the GitHub Actions postgres:16 SERVICE CONTAINER credentials, defined in the same file, and pr-gate.yml already carries three identical lines - pre-existing convention, not a secret. INC-02 OWNER DECISION NEEDED: rotate the `postgres` superuser password on the Windows DB VPS 103.118.16.189. Arguments for: security-baseline.md says a secret that appears in a durable log must be rotated, the transcript persists on disk, and this repo has rotated this exact credential before (T-252, 2026-08-21). INC-02 MECHANISM, second occurrence so it is owed now rather than optional: the standing brief line 'never write a password into any file, read it inline' is insufficient - it does not stop a worker PRINTING one while searching for it. The brief line must become: never grep GLOBAL.env for credential VALUES; read the one key you need by exact name into a variable in the same command and never print the result. A redaction regex that only covers KEY=value misses the inline URL form, which is how this one escaped.

item-01: AT ITEM CLOSE, add to the card Known gaps section (docs PR), with these CORRECTED numbers: 10 production rows carry a published issue_size with zero field_sources rows, all created between 2025-12 and 2026-03, none since. Not 39 and not ongoing - an earlier measurement of mine counted 28 seed rows with issue_size=0 as published values and mistook their recent created_at for current behaviour. The cause is data-persister.ts::upsertIPO's fallback door (~lines 1330-1385), which fires when consolidateIPOData throws and sets fieldSourcesWritten:false unconditionally by design. The create door (~line 1406) gates on ENABLE_SOURCE_TRACKING, which defaults false in code but is set true in both shared/env/prod/scraper.env and shared/env/staging/scraper.env, correctly symlinked - so the card's claim that these flags are already on in prod is TRUE and item 1's premise holds. Tracked as #454. Worth noting on the card that the fallback door writes data without provenance SILENTLY - no log, no error - which is the part worth a later check.
